'''Mitaka Shrine''' (みたかじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Mitaka, {{ill|Kawazu, Shizuoka|arz|كاوازو|ceb|Kawazu Chō|es|Kawazu|fa|کاوازو، شیزوئوکا|fr|Kawazu|id|Kawazu, Shizuoka|it|Kawazu|ja|河津町|ko|가와즈정|ms|Kawazu, Shizuoka|my|ခဝဇုမြို့|pl|Kawazu|ru|Кавадзу|tl|Kawazu, Shizuoka|tr|Kawazu|uk|Кавадзу (Сідзуока)|ur|کاوازو، شیزوکا|vi|Kawazu, Shizuoka|zh|河津町|qid=Q1203861}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Shizuoka|Q961511|qid=Q961511}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}.<ref name="jinjacho">[http://shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4401013 Mitaka Shrine] – Shizuoka Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines</ref>

=== Overview ===
The shrine is situated in the easternmost Mitaka district of Kawazu Town, in the mountainous area to the east overlooking the Shimokawazu Fishing Port and Mitaka Beach. It stands adjacent to the southwest of the former Kawazu Town Higashi Elementary School, near {{ill|Imaihama-Kaigan Station|ja|今井浜海岸駅|ko|이마이하마카이간역|my|အိမအိဟမ - ခိုင်းဂန်ဘူတာ|zh|今井濱海岸站|qid=Q6002975}}, {{ill|Japan National Route 135|af|Japan Nasionale Roete 135|ja|国道135号|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Kok-tō 135-hō|qid=Q6156779}}, and just east of {{ill|Imaihama Beach|Q11376648|qid=Q11376648|lt=Imaihama Coast}}.

According to tradition, the shrine was founded in {{ill|Tenpyō|br|Tenpyō|ca|Era Tenpyō|de|Tempyō|es|Tenpyō|fa|تنپیو|fr|Ère Tenpyō|ia|Tenpyo|id|Tempyō|it|Tenpyō|ja|天平|ko|덴표|no|Tenpyō|pt|Tenpyō|ru|Тэмпё|simple|Tenpyō|sr|Тенпјо|tr|Tenpyō|uk|Темпьо (ненґо)|zh|天平 (日本)|zh_yue|天平 (日本)|qid=Q1199879}} 5 ({{ill|733|ab|733|af|733|am|733 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|733|ar|733|ary|733|ast|733|az|733|azb|۷۳۳ (میلادی)|be|733|be_x_old|733|bg|733|bn|৭৩৩|bpy|মারি ৭৩৩|br|733|bs|733.|ca|733|cdo|733 nièng|ceb|733|ckb|٧٣٣|crh|733|cs|733|cv|733|cy|733|da|733|de|733|el|733|eml|733|eo|733|es|733|et|733|eu|733|fa|۷۳۳ (میلادی)|fi|733|fo|733|fr|733|fy|733|ga|733|gan|733年|gd|733|gl|733|gv|733|he|733|hi|733|hr|733.|ht|733 (almanak jilyen)|hu|733|hy|733|id|733|io|733|is|733|it|733|ja|733年|jv|733|ka|733|kaa|733|kk|733 жыл|ko|733년|la|733|lb|733|lij|733|lmo|733|lt|733 m.|map_bms|733|mdf|733|mg|733|mhr|733|mk|733|mr|इ.स. ७३३|mrj|733 и|ms|733|mzn|۷۳۳|nah|733|nap|733|nds|733|new|सन् ७३३|nl|733|nn|733|no|733|nov|733|nrm|733|nso|733|oc|733|or|୭୩୩|os|733-æм аз|pl|733|pnb|733|pt|733|qu|733|ro|733|ru|733 год|rue|733|sa|७३३|scn|733|sd|733ع|sh|733.|shn|733|si|733|simple|733|sk|733|sl|733|smn|733|sq|733|sr|733|su|733|sv|733|sw|733|tg|Соли 733|th|พ.ศ. 1276|tk|733|tl|733|tly|733|tr|733|tt|733 ел|uk|733|ur|733ء|uz|733|vec|733|vi|733|war|733|wuu|733年|xmf|733|zh|733年|zh_min_nan|733 nî|zh_yue|733年|qid=Q23570}}), and it is considered a candidate shrine (ronsha) for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} '''Takeishitsuki no Mikoto Shrine'''.<ref>[https://shrineheritager.com/mitaka-shrine/ Mitaka Shrine] – Shrine-heritager</ref><ref name="yuisho">Shrine precinct origin inscription</ref>

Based on the founding legend of Mimitaka Daimyōjin riding on an ox, the grand annual festival held on October 22–23 includes the custom of offering “Shitabera-mochi.” In addition, there is a tradition of performing the {{ill|Shiki Sanban|Q11254805|qid=Q11254805}} ({{ill|Sanbasō|Q11356796|qid=Q11356796}}), dedicated in the shrine’s kagura hall. This tradition was formed with the involvement of the locally born {{ill|Kabuki|Q199701|qid=Q199701}} actors {{ill|Ichikawa Kodanji IV|Q11480242|qid=Q11480242|lt=4th Ichikawa Kodanji}} and his adopted son {{ill|Ichikawa Sadanji I|Q11480254|qid=Q11480254|lt=1st Ichikawa Sadanji}}, and it has been designated an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Kawazu Town.<ref name="yuisho"/><ref name="kanko">[https://www.kawazu-onsen.com/sightseeing/41 Mitaka Shrine] – Kawazu Town Tourism Association</ref><ref name="joho">[https://shizuoka-hamamatsu-izu.com/event/mitakasikisannbasou/ Mitaka Shiki Sanbasō] – Shizuoka, Hamamatsu, Izu Information Bureau</ref>
